_doc: Canonical symbol map: semantic name -> Ravenswatch engine function/global. This is the source of truth (like Minecraft mappings). Ghidra names, the loader C++ header, and the Python SDK constants are all GENERATED from this file via `rsmm symbols gen`. Resolution: `raw` joins to data/function_patterns.json by name for version-resilient (byte-pattern) lookup; `anchor` is an inlined routine reached as parent_pattern + offset; `va` is a base-relative absolute (data globals, which have no code pattern). `status`: ok = pattern/anchor resolvable in the current corpus; va = base-relative only; unverified = documented in an older corpus, not yet re-confirmed against the shipped pattern DB.

symbols.name: Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent
symbols.signature: void(void* analytics_mgr, void* payload_kv, StringDesc* event_name, char has_run_ctx)
symbols.note: CENTRAL TELEMETRY SINK. ~37 gameplay callers funnel named analytics events through here (run_end, enemy_killed, matchmaking_start, level_up_reach, level_up_book, ...), each building a key-value payload then submitting as JSON (projectId 'passtech-ravenswatch') to Passtech's analytics backend over an authenticated HTTP POST. param_3 is a StringDesc { const char* ptr @+0x0; uint32 len|0x80000000 @+0x8 } holding the event name. The loader 'firehose' detour (hook_events.cpp::install_analytics_firehose) reads that name and re-publishes it to the Lua bus by its raw name, so ONE hook exposes every named event to mods (R.on('enemy_killed', cb)) and survives the game adding new event names. OBSERVATION-GRADE: these fire AFTER the gameplay action and carry analytics KV, not live entity handles — good for 'when X happens do Y' triggers, not for mutating the actor. For entity-context gameplay events (damage, give-item) see the oCGameNamedEvent bus — mapped: NamedEvent_Dispatch is the single hook point (R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'), docs/_re/kinds/events-bus.md). Skips 'run_end' to avoid double-firing the typed Event_RunEnd table hook. [2026-07-10: recovered via anchor/decompile-verify (batch 2) after the July-9 remap mis-placed it.]

symbols.name: NamedEvent_Dispatch
symbols.note: THE oCGameNamedEvent bus dispatch — one detour here exposes every entity-context gameplay event (NETWORK_DAMAGE, GIVE_MAGICAL_OBJECT, GAIN_REROLL, ...) with a live payload. dispatcher = the NamedEventDispatcher sub-object (entity+0x4d8 for entity events; world+0x340 for world events; channel map at dispatcher+0x28, dispatch queue at +0x00..0x18, re-entrancy guard at +0x60). Clones the event (vcall ev+0x18), enqueues the clone, then (unless re-entrant) drains the queue: find-only channel lookup (NamedEvent_ChannelMap_Find) by *(u32*)(ev+0x30), iterates the node's sub array setting the node+0x18 cursor, invokes (*(sub+0x10))(ev, sub) per subscriber, handles mid-dispatch self-unsubscribe (cursor == -1), erases empty channels, deletes the clone (NamedEvent_Delete). Event header (all classes): vft @+0x00, u32 2 @+0x08, name String {char* @+0x20, u32 cap|0x80000000 @+0x28, u32 len @+0x2c}, u32 interned id @+0x30 — so the hook reads the PLAINTEXT name straight off the event. Loader detour: hook_events.cpp::install_gameplay_bus (RSMM_ENABLE_GAMEPLAY_EVENTS=1), published as R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'). Also the local-emit primitive: construct an event and call this directly (the give-MO path in FUN_140397190 does exactly that). [2026-07-10: recovered via live-Ghidra decompile-verified anchor/call-graph after the July-9 remap mis-placed it mid-instruction.]

symbols.name: NamedEvent_Id_FromCrc
symbols.note: Interned event-id derivation: id = crc32 over the 8 bytes of (ns, name_crc) interleaved byte-wise (standard reflected crc32 table). Event names are interned at static-init as id = NamedEvent_Id_FromCrc(0, crc32(name)) — so the loader can derive the id for ANY event name at runtime (used by the Lua gameplay-emit primitive). VERIFIED 2026-06-14: the crc table is built by Crc32_TableInit with polynomial 0x04C11DB7 (reflected) = the standard CRC32 table (0xEDB88320); the byte feed order is [ns.b0, crc.b0, ns.b1, crc.b1, ns.b2, crc.b2, ns.b3, crc.b3], init 0xffffffff, final invert. Id_HashString is the runtime one-call form (crc32(name) then this). NOTE: this is the NAMED-EVENT/string id scheme only — the entity-value store (EntityValue_Lookup) keys are NOT these (they are structured/sequential ids, e.g. 0x12e831f3/0x12e831f4 adjacent — impossible for independent CRCs). [2026-07-10: DOWNGRADED — July-9 remap address resolves mid-instruction; no confident anchor. Pattern stripped -> loader fails closed. Needs manual RE.]

symbols.name: Id_HashString
symbols.note: Runtime string -> 32-bit id hasher: standard CRC32 over the name bytes (init 0xffffffff, table from Crc32_TableInit), then id = NamedEvent_Id_FromCrc(0, ~runningCrc). Lazily builds the crc table on first use (guard byte DAT_1414366f3). Used by def deserializers to intern a name string into an id (stored e.g. at hero+0x140). The Python equivalent is in data/ tooling-verifiable: id = crc32_pair(0, crc32(name)). Confirms how event/name ids are derived from strings; does NOT generate entity-VALUE-store keys (those are structured ids). [2026-07-09 patch: prologue changed, not re-confirmed; needs manual RE.]

symbols.name: Entity_DispatchHit
symbols.note: LOCAL damage/hit application — the enemy-damage counterpart to Entity_ModifyHealth (which is hero-only). param_1 = the TARGET entity; its hit component lives inline (mutex @+0x498, hit-handler list {base @+0x4b0, count @+0x4b8}, reentrancy guard @+0x4c0, pending-hit array {base @+0x4c8, count @+0x4d0, cap @+0x4d4}). param_2 = a fully-built oCEntityHitData (~0xb0 bytes: vft @+0x0, source/instigator entity* @+0x10, copied hit floats/vectors @+0x18..0x90, target entity* @+0xa0; the two entity ptrs are accessed through their vtables, so must be live oCEntity handles). When no hit handler is mid-dispatch it runs the target's hit handlers immediately, otherwise it memcpy-queues a 0xb0 hit-data copy into the pending array. Called by NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit for self/non-networked targets. ENEMY-DAMAGE BLOCKER: there is no low-arity 'damage entity by amount' primitive — both this and the network path require constructing a complete oCEntityHitData with valid source+target handles, which is the real work item for offensive tier-2. Helpers: FUN_1403124b0(entity)=net/replication state (returns obj whose +0x130 byte = is-remote flag), FUN_140726330(entity)=source net-id. [2026-07-10: recovered via live-Ghidra decompile-verified anchor/call-graph after the July-9 remap mis-placed it mid-instruction.]

symbols.name: Entity_GetNetComponent
symbols.note: SwissTable/F14 component-map lookup on an entity for the fixed type-id 0x154fce5c (the net/replication component). Probes the entity's component map (control bytes @entity+0x5e8, slots @entity+0x5f0, bucket mask @entity+0x600) and returns the component pointer, or 0 if the entity has none (e.g. single-player / non-replicated). The returned component's byte @+0x130 is the local/remote AUTHORITY flag: 0 = locally controlled (this client owns the entity and emits its NETWORK_DAMAGE), nonzero = remotely controlled (apply received state, don't emit). Both hit paths (NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit, the attack resolver FUN_1403dc780) gate network emit on this flag. NOTE: it dereferences the component map unconditionally, so only call on a known-valid entity. Pattern is multi-match (index 3/6, 128-byte sig) — fn_verify-guarded. Relevant to local-vs-remote hero disambiguation in co-op, though hero-capture already pins the local player via the HUD-mirror requirement (only the local player has one). [2026-07-10: recovered via live-Ghidra decompile-verified anchor/call-graph after the July-9 remap mis-placed it mid-instruction.]

symbols.name: Entity_LookupMagicalObjectComponent
symbols.signature: void*(void* componentStore, void** out, oCEntity* entity)
symbols.note: Read-only F14/SwissTable lookup that maps an entity to its owned magical-object component. Called at the top of Hero_GrantMagicalObject (FUN_140397030): store = *(entity+8), key = entity; it FNV-1a-hashes the entity pointer, probes the store's control bytes @store+0x1d0 / slots @store+0x1d8 / mask @store+0x1e8, writes the component pointer (or 0 when absent) into *out and returns out. Side-effect-free. Non-null ONLY for entities that can own magical objects (heroes) — pets, summons and enemies are not registered in the store and resolve to 0. The loader uses this as the grant-target discriminator so R.give's dispatcher capture (rsmm.lua) accepts only a real hero's dispatcher, not a summon's, fixing item-grant on summon heroes (Piper/Scarlet/Geppetto) where an anchor event fired from a pet dispatcher used to clobber _give_hero. Decompile-verified 2026-07-12.

symbols.name: Entity_ResolveAttackHits
symbols.signature: float(void* attacker, uint hitDefIndex, TargetList* targets, float damageMul, float baseDamage)
symbols.note: Attack-resolution / multi-target hit applier — the real producer that builds an oCEntityHitData per target and calls Entity_DispatchHit. param_1 = attacker context (its hit-def array @+0xd8, entity @+0x8); param_2 = index into that hit-def array; param_3 = target list {count @+0x0, entity** @+0x8}; param_4 = damage multiplier; param_5 = base damage (if <=0, pulled from the hit-def's value object). Per target it: allocs a hit handle (FUN_140214f30, released by NamedEvent_Delete), stack-builds the 0xb0 oCEntityHitData (vft=oCEntityHitData_vftable, 4 constant template vectors from 0x140fc6c10/6c50/6e70/7240, hit-value obj* whose +0x8 = the damage, attacker @ a slot, target position from target.vtable[+0x48], source net-id via Entity_GetNetComponent), then Entity_DispatchHit(target, hitData). THE ENEMY-DAMAGE ENTRY POINT: there is no standalone oCEntityHitData ctor — construction is inlined here and needs a real attacker hit-def, so synthesizing a hit from nothing is impractical. The viable mod path is to HOOK this and AMPLIFY/redirect: scale the hit-value damage (*(hitval+0x8)) or swap the target list. See docs/_re/kinds/enemy-damage.md. [2026-07-10: recovered via live-Ghidra decompile-verified anchor/call-graph after the July-9 remap mis-placed it mid-instruction.]

symbols.name: Entity_ModifyHealth
symbols.signature: void(oCEntity* hero, float delta, oCCustomFlagList* sourceTags)
symbols.note: Core HP-modification routine on the hero CHARACTER object (delta>0 heals, delta<0 damages) — the engine's own heal/damage primitive, with clamping, the UI mirror write, analytics submit, and the gained/lost named-event cascade. IMPORTANT: hero is NOT the bus dispatcher and NOT dispatcher-0x4d8 (that was a wrong guess that crashed; the dispatcher and the hero character are separate heap objects). The hero is baked into each event subscription as the handler's param_1 — capture it by hooking a hero-bound handler (Entity_GainHealthHandler / Entity_GiveHandler, both param_1=hero, pointer-only sigs). HERO HEALTH LAYOUT: current HP f32 @hero+0x15c8, max HP f32 @hero+0x15cc, missing-health ratio @+0x15d0, UI/display mirror pointer @hero+0x1d80 (the routine writes new HP to both +0x15c8 and *(*(hero+0x1d80))). HERO-ONLY — DO NOT call on enemies: param_1+0x1d80 (the HUD mirror) is dereferenced UNCONDITIONALLY for any nonzero delta (`**(param_1+0x1d80)=newHP`, plus `*(*(param_1+0x1d80)+0x10)` on heal and a +0x1db0 secondary mirror) — an enemy/non-player entity has no HUD mirror there, so calling this on one access-violates. Enemy damage must use a different path (the hit-data network-damage event NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit / oCGameNamedEventNetworkDamage, which carries a full oCEntityHitData), NOT this routine. R.combat is therefore correctly hero-scoped. sourceTags = an oCCustomFlagList ctx (vftable @va 0x140efc320, then {list=0, count=0}); an EMPTY flag list {vftable,0,0} is accepted. Verified by decompiling the inbound GAIN_HEALTH handler FUN_1403993f0, which calls this twice: damage = ModifyHealth(hero, -amt, tags{'Damage'}), heal = ModifyHealth(hero, +amt, tags). Exposed via R.entity / R.combat in rsmm.lua. Float arg requires the (ptr,float,ptr) prototype added to fn_call.cpp. [2026-07-09 patch: prologue changed, not re-confirmed; needs manual RE.] [2026-07-09: recovered — (hero,float) sig, heal/damage sign-branch, hero+0x1d80 carrier, decompile-verified.]

Early-outs if the level is unchanged. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: XpComponent_IsMaxLevel
symbols.note: The gate at the top of Hero_GainExperience: walks the component's +0x110 next-link chain to the LAST node, reads max level (GetMaxLevel logic: +0x70 object [+8], else inline data at +0x68, clamped to >=1), and returns (last node's level >= max). Returns via `setae al` so only the LOW BYTE of the return is meaningful -- mask with &0xff. When true, Hero_GainExperience returns without applying any XP, which is why a grant on a component with no max-level config (max clamps to 1, level starts at 1) silently no-ops. Disasm-verified live 2026-07-19.

symbols.name: XpComponent_GetMaxLevel
symbols.note: Max level for an XP/GroupLevel component: walks the +0x110 next-link chain to the last node, then reads the max-level from the +0x70 object ([+8]) or, when +0x70 is null, from the inline small-string/variant data at +0x68; result clamped to >=1. A component with neither configured reports 1 -- which makes level-1 heroes 'at max' and turns Hero_GainExperience into a no-op. Disasm-verified live 2026-07-19.

symbols.name: XpComponent_XpForLevel
symbols.note: XP threshold to complete `level` (arg2): walks the +0x110 chain to the last node, reads the curve config at *(node+0x10) -- when flag +0x1d0 is set and level <= count (+0x1e0) returns table[level-1] from the array at +0x1d8, otherwise the last table entry, or 0xffffffff when the table is empty. The per-level thresholds Hero_GainExperience's level-up loop consumes. Disasm-verified live 2026-07-19.

symbols.note: Sets the XP component's current-xp-within-level (*(xpComp+0x108)[+4]) and, when xp increased, writes custom-flag key 0x12e831f1 (=xp delta, f32). Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.note: Linear-scan getComponent: walks the entity component array (entity+0x190, count entity+0x198) and returns the first component whose class IsKindOf the given type-tester vtable. entity = *(heroController+0x2f8). Simplest way to fetch a sibling component (e.g. the XpComponent via XpComponent_TypeTester). Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.note: Fast getComponent: resolves a component through the entity's type->index hash map (entity+0x28), then confirms with a virtual IsKindOf ((*(type+0x58))(type, tester)). arg2 = type-tester, arg3 = 32-bit type key. Prefer Entity_GetComponentByTester when the exact key is unknown. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: XpComponent_vftable
symbols.note: Vftable of the hero's XP/level component. CORRECTED 2026-07-18 from 0x140f23200, which was NOT a vtable: it lands 0x50 INSIDE this vtable (slot 10 of 30), so the exact-match scan `*(comp)==va` could never hit -- that single constant is why R.xp returned nil across 5 playtests. Real class is oCDtEntityCpntGroupLevel (hash 0x15888c02, size 0x170, ctor 0x1402e1de0); there is no `Xp*` class in the 5993-vtable dump. CONFIRMED 2026-07-19: the component is NOT on the hero -- exactly one instance exists, on EntitySettings/Common_Settings/Group_Scaling.entity.ot ('[Dt Group Level] Group_Scaling\\Hero Group'), which is why component scans of hero entities found nothing. Progress is a POINTER at +0x108 -> {u32 level @0, u32 xp @4}. Reachable via the game-scene-context registry (ctx+0x58 array, +0x60 count), not by entity walking. Symbol keeps the XpComponent_* name for loader/SDK compatibility.

symbols.name: XpComponent_TypeTester
symbols.note: Type-tester global (DAT_141476e00) used by the XP component's own IsKindOf/parent-resolution; pass as arg2 to Entity_GetComponentByTester to fetch the hero XpComponent. Sibling tester DAT_141476d48. Confidence medium (tester provenance) — the vtable scan via XpComponent_vftable is the fallback. Verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: EntityValueStore_Recompute
symbols.note: Recomputes the entity-value override CACHE (store+0xc0 vector, the same one R.stat.set pokes) from scratch: seeds each key with its base value from the definition (valueDef+0xc8/+0xd0), then walks the per-key modifier registry (SwissTable at store+0x88: ctrl @+0x88, slots @+0x90, growth @+0xa0) and applies every registered modifier in priority order via a vcall on the modifier object (`(*(modifier+0x18))(modifier, valueUnion)`), writing the folded result back into the override entry (union @entry+0x08, scalar mirror @entry+0x28, version short @entry+0x2c). Gated by the dirty flag store+0x64 bit 3 (&8). THIS IS WHY a raw R.stat.set union-poke is transient: the next recompute (any gameplay event that dirties the key) rebuilds entry+0x08 from base+modifiers and discards the poke. Durable writes must register a modifier the recompute folds in — see EntityValueStore_ApplyModifierEvent. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: EntityValueStore_ApplyModifierEvent
symbols.signature: void(void* store, void* modifierEvent, void* a3, void* a4)
symbols.note: The engine's DURABLE add-a-stat-modifier routine. Reads the modifier request (built by ModifierEvent_Ctor into an oCGameEventNetworkModifier, vftable 0x140f322d0), constructs an oCEntityValueModifier (flag@+0x30=1, id@+0x38, value union@+0x08, amount f32@+0x3c, base f32@+0x40, subscriber list @+0x570), inserts it into the per-key modifier registry (store+0x88 SwissTable), then re-folds the override cache entry (store+0xc0 via EntityValueOverride_Alloc) so the new value takes effect immediately AND survives recompute. Combine mode `op` (read from the value-def @+0x68) selects the fold: 1=ADDITIVE (val += amount*scale), 2=SET (override value + base), 3=MATCH-REPLACE (replace a modifier with the same source/id), 4=MIN/priority (keep smallest-delta). This is the correct entry point for a permanent stat change. NOTE: param_2 is a fully-built modifier event; wiring from Lua needs the event payload (op/key/amount, id@+0x54, the virtual fill at def+0x20) decoded + a live playtest before it can be trusted engine-mutating. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: EntityValueStore_InitBaseValues
symbols.note: Store bootstrap: registers three internal event listeners (stored at store+0x168/+0x170/+0x178 via the event pool at entity+0x500), then, for a magical-object-owning entity (Entity_LookupMagicalObjectComponent non-null), seeds the override cache (store+0xc0) from the base value defs and the initial modifier set — the same fold EntityValueStore_Recompute performs, run once at setup. Confirms the store layout used by the R.stat path: keys @store+0x88 registry, cache @store+0xc0/count+0xc8. Read-only reference for durable-modifier wiring. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: ModifierEvent_Ctor
symbols.note: In-place ctor of an oCGameEventNetworkModifier (the durable stat-modifier named event; object carries a modifier request through the same named-event bus R.give uses). Sets the vft chain oCGameNamedEvent (0x140f05aa8) -> ...Network (0x140f09d98) -> oCGameEventNetworkModifier (0x140f322d0), u32 2@+0x08, event id@+0x30 (from valueDef+0x54), default union@+0x60 (EntityValueUnion_DefaultCtor), scale f32 1.0 @+0x84 and @+0x88, byte 1@+0x8c, then calls the value-def's virtual fill `(*(valueDef+0x20))(valueDef, event)` to populate op/key/amount, and clears u32@+0x08. Feed the built event to EntityValueStore_ApplyModifierEvent (or dispatch it via NamedEvent_Dispatch to the entity's dispatcher) to apply a durable modifier. Decompile-verified live 2026-07-13.

symbols.name: oCGameEventNetworkModifier_vftable
symbols.note: vftable of oCGameEventNetworkModifier — the durable stat-modifier named event (leaf of the oCGameNamedEvent -> ...Network -> Modifier chain). Set as the third/most-derived vftable by ModifierEvent_Ctor. Identifies a modifier event when scanning the named-event bus; anchor for building a durable-stat-modifier event from the loader. Verified live 2026-07-13 (LEA @0x14038a01d in ModifierEvent_Ctor).

_event_catalog_doc: Observation events the loader republishes by raw name from the central telemetry sink (Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent). No address — the firehose detour reads the name at runtime, so any name the game adds also fires even if absent here. These are confirmed names harvested by string-xref (cluster 0x140f13a00-0x140f13f00); subscribe via R.on('<name>', cb) with RSMM_ENABLE_GAME_EVENTS=1. Shown by `rsmm symbols events`.
